title: Tool schema error classification and recovery patterns for function-call parameters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: function/tool calling currently suffers from ambiguous error messages when client-sent parameters don't match the declared JSON schema, and from inconsistent behavior during streaming responses. This ticket defines a recommended JSON schema definition format for tool parameters, a clear error taxonomy for validation/runtime mismatches, and the client recovery patterns to use in both non-streaming and streaming contexts.

Goals:
- Standardize a compact, compatible schema shape that SDKs and runtime can consume with minimal transformation.
- Produce machine-friendly error codes and human-friendly messages for validation failures and runtime conversion errors.
- Define streaming semantics when parameter validation fails after partial output is streamed (how to surface warnings vs. terminal errors).
- Provide acceptance criteria and backward-compatible migration notes for existing tool contract formats.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A one-page JSON schema convention doc (example included below) that is implementable in the runtime and SDKs.
2) Error taxonomy with canonical error codes and recommended HTTP mappings.
3) SDK semantics documented for 3 client recovery flows: fail-fast, best-effort-coercion-with-warning, and server-side-fallback-to-defaults.
4) E2E tests and a new CI validation job verifying schema->runtime validation sanity.

Proposed compact schema convention (human-readable, JSON string below is intentionally compact to reduce payload in tooling payloads):

EXAMPLE_SCHEMA_SNIPPET:
{
  "name": "createInvoice",
  "description": "Create an invoice from line items",
  "params": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "customer_id": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "internal customer UUID"
      },
      "lines": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "description": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "amount_cents": {
              "type": "integer",
              "minimum": 0
            }
          },
          "required": ["description", "amount_cents"]
        }
      },
      "currency": {
        "type": "string",
        "enum": ["USD", "EUR"],
        "default": "USD"
      }
    },
    "required": ["customer_id", "lines"]
  }
}

Notes on the schema convention:
- Keep to JSON Schema core (draft-07 compatible subset); avoid oneOf/anyOf for top-level parameter shapes where possible because runtime coercion and error reporting are harder to unify. If oneOf is unavoidable, require a discriminant field.
- Support an optional "coercionHints" array at property-level (string tokens describing safe conversions e.g., "number-from-string", "trim-whitespace"). This is a lightweight extension that SDKs can opt into.
- Encourage inclusion of "enum" + "default" for fields that have well-known fallback choices to enable server-side fallback.

Error taxonomy (canonical codes and recommended mapping):
- VALIDATION_ERROR: schema-level validation failure (missing required, type mismatch, pattern mismatch). Recommended HTTP mapping: 400 Bad Request. Machine field: "error_code": "VALIDATION_ERROR".
- PARAM_COERCION_WARNING: client provided value coerced successfully (e.g., "\"123\" -> 123"). Map to 200 but include "warnings" array in metadata. Machine field: "error_code": "PARAM_COERCION_WARNING".
- RUNTIME_CAST_ERROR: passed validation but runtime failed to cast/serialize into model inputs (e.g., very large integer overflow). Recommended mapping: 422 Unprocessable Entity and an "error_code".
- TOOL_SCHEMA_MISMATCH: tool definition incompatible with runtime capabilities (e.g., unsupported type like "binary" without explicit handling). Recommended mapping: 500 Internal Server Error with guidance to contact support.
- STREAM_ABORTED_BY_VALIDATION: streaming response started and later request-level validation discovered a fatal mismatch. Recommended semantics: server streams a final control frame with "error_code" and an explicit "stream_status": "aborted". Client should treat as terminal.

Suggested error payload shape (stringified example to be parsed by SDKs):
{
  "error_code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "message": "Parameter 'lines[0].amount_cents' must be an integer >= 0",
  "path": "lines.0.amount_cents",
  "hint": "Send as integer cents; received '12.34'"
}

Streaming-specific recovery patterns:
- Fail-fast (default): Validate full params before generating tokens. If validation fails, return VALIDATION_ERROR with 400 and do not start streaming. Pros: deterministic. Cons: higher latency for schemas that require server-side enrichment.
- Stream-with-warnings: Start streaming early, perform progressive validation of fields as they are resolved. If a coercion happens, emit a metadata/warning chunk inline and continue. If a fatal error occurs mid-stream, emit STREAM_ABORTED_BY_VALIDATION control frame and end stream. Clients must handle partial outputs and final status. Pros: lower latency. Cons: more complex client handling.
- Server-fallbacks: If enum/defaults are present, server may substitute defaults and continue, emitting PARAM_COERCION_WARNING. This should only be allowed for low-risk parameters (config flags, locale, currency).

Migration notes and compatibility:
- Existing tool contracts that use openapi-style schemas will continue to be accepted. Add a lightweight translation layer at the runtime ingress to convert OpenAPI constructs into the compact convention.
- We must NOT silently change semantics of existing tools: if translation leads to ambiguous behavior, runtime should surface a TOOL_SCHEMA_MISMATCH advisory during the migration window and opt tools into new behavior per-tool.

Testing and telemetry requirements:
- Add unit tests that assert canonical error codes are produced for offending inputs.
- Add an integration test harness that simulates streaming aborts and verifies final control frame shapes.
- Add console dashboard metrics: validation_errors_per_tool, coercion_warnings_rate, stream_aborts_per_hour.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Draft spec and short RFC (this ticket). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TOOL/Function+Call+Schema+Error+Spec (placeholder).
2) Runtime ingress: implement compact-schema parser and error classification.
3) SDKs: emit clearer developer warnings and expose an opt-in streaming-with-warnings mode.
4) CI: add schema linting job and telemetry dashboards.

Deliverables:
- This RFC in Confluence (link above).
- Runtime PR with tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824 (WIP).
- SDK changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/948 (draft).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full OpenAPI importer (will be a follow-up), detailed UX copy for warning messages in Console (small follow-up).

2026-02-25 - Lena Cho: Security review requested. We need to ensure default fallbacks aren't used for sensitive fields (PII identifiers) without explicit allowlist. Suggest adding a 'noFallback' property for sensitive params.
